newsitem.title: ITALY: Lira ERM return must not affect euro effort-Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: Lira ERM return must not affect euro effort-Ciampi.

text.p: Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Tuesday that the lira's return to Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM) must not affect Italy's efforts to meet criteria for membership of planned European monetary union.

"We need to be very aware that re-entry in the ERM is something very different from entry into the single European currency," Ciampi told the Senate (upper house) budget committee. "We cannot reduce our commitment because it is not easy to meet the (euro) criteria."
The lira returned to the ERM grid after a four-year absence at a central rate of 990 per mark following tough talks over the weekend among European Union finance ministers in Brussels.

Italy hopes to be among founding members which will enter the euro on January 1, 1999. The government's 1997 budget aims to slash 62.5 trillion lire from next year's deficit to come close to the three per cent deficit to Gross Domestic Product ratio required for euro membership.
